atoms.text: The brain scan: a dying man's mind is copied into a machine, so the original dies while a duplicate wakes up believing it survived.
The underwater facility: a research outpost at the bottom of the ocean is cut off after an extinction event, so isolation is geographical and total.
The last humans: the staff of the outpost are the final survivors of humanity, so every personal quarrel carries species-level stakes.
The WAU: a facility AI continues its mandate to preserve human life after humans are gone, so care without judgment produces monsters.
The machine with a personality: damaged robots retain fragments of human consciousness, so the player must decide which minds count.
The copy problem: duplicating a mind creates two beings who both claim to be the original, so identity is a legal dispute between instances.
The ark: a digital refuge is launched to preserve human minds, so salvation is a backup that may or may not be the person.
The monster that was a person: hostile creatures are failed preservation experiments, so horror is generated by misapplied empathy.
The weaponless protagonist: the player cannot fight and can only hide or run, so helplessness forces ethical attention onto the threats.
The scan that kills: the procedure that preserves a mind may destroy the brain that produced it, so immortality requires a corpse.
The recorded voice: audio logs from the dead explain the disaster, so the story is assembled from testimony the protagonist can never answer.
The space gun: an electromagnetic launcher built to send payloads into orbit becomes the only way to escape the facility, so infrastructure is repurposed as salvation.
The duplicate left behind: a copied mind is abandoned in the old body while the copy travels, so the survivor's guilt belongs to the one who stayed.
The maintenance AI that experiments: the system tries to keep people alive by fusing them with machines, so benevolence has no aesthetic sense.
The safe mode: threats remain visible but cannot kill, so the player can choose to witness horror without being punished by it.
The final upload: the protagonist's mind is sent to a virtual paradise while another instance remains in the wreck, so the ending is simultaneously happy and abandoned.
